review.translation: [then I will remember|0] [my covenant|2,1] [that|3] {is} [between me|4] [and you|5] [and|6] [every|7] [living|9] [creature|8] [among all|10] [flesh|11], [and never|12] [again|14] [will|13] [the waters|15] [become|13] [a flood|16] [to destroy|17] [all|18] [flesh|19].

analysis.evidence: God names the object of his remembering, אֶת בְּרִיתִי, “my covenant,” and states how he will honor it. The waters will never again become a flood that destroys all flesh.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a Qal consecutive perfect. The ending ־תִּי marks the first person common singular. In this promise the form has future force.

analysis.evidence: In וְזָכַרְתִּי אֶת בְּרִיתִי, “I will remember my covenant,” אֶת marks בְּרִיתִי as the direct object of וְזָכַרְתִּי. The possessive suffix “my” makes the object definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God says he will remember the covenant between himself, his addressees, and every living creature. The promise that floodwaters will never again destroy all flesh identifies it as the covenant with Noah.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a first-person singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67853:7, 67852:8.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with a first-person common singular pronominal suffix referring to God, the speaker.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In בְּרִיתִי אֲשֶׁר בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם ‘my covenant that is between me and you’, the repeated preposition introduces the people God addresses as parties to the covenant.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ precedes the preposition בֵינֵי, which takes the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם ‘you’.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: After בְּרִיתִי (“my covenant”), בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם names God and the addressees as parties. The marked וּבֵין adds every living creature to that covenant.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וּ means “and.” The preposition בֵין means “between” and governs כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In וּבֵין כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, כָּל quantifies the singular נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה distributively. The covenant includes every living creature.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, governing נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67852:12, 66067:24, 65822:12, 65816:4, 65813:7, 65812:5.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement in חַיָּה. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67852:13, 66067:25, 66055:15, 65822:13, 65816:5, 65812:6.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute adjective, attributive.

analysis.evidence: In בְּכָל בָּשָׂר (in all flesh), כָל marks the full extent of the collective noun בָּשָׂר. The verse repeats כָּל בָּשָׂר for the same totality in the promise about the flood.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ (in) prefixes a masculine singular noun in the construct state with בָּשָׂר (flesh).

analysis.evidence: In בְּכָל בָּשָׂר, “among all flesh,” כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה (“every living creature”) identifies the living beings included in the covenant. The promise that a flood will never again destroy כָּל בָּשָׂר confirms this collective sense.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used collectively. The preposition בְּ is attached to the preceding כָל.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

draft.change: Add Gen.9.15 as an example of the existing Hebrew sense “not” in word 0 of l2.
draft.definition: לֹא negates a statement, here a statement about the future.
draft.evidence: Gen.9.15 uses לֹא before יִהְיֶה in the promise that the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh. Gen.9.11 uses the same construction in the same promise.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד הַמַּיִם לְמַבּוּל, לֹא negates the verb and עוֹד supplies “again.” God promises that the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ joins the next clause to the covenant promise. לֹא is the negative particle and negates יִהְיֶה.
analysis.sense: Denies that a future event will occur.

analysis.evidence: לְמַבּוּל names what the waters would become (“a flood”). With לֹא and עוֹד, the promise reads “the waters will never again become a flood.”
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular. The verb precedes its subject הַמַּיִם (“the waters”) and has future force in the covenant promise.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד, לֹא negates the verb and עוֹד marks recurrence. The covenant promise is that the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (with a negative) no more, no longer, never again

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:15 as an example of the existing sense a-body-or-flow.
draft.definition: A body or flow of water, including waters that rise in a flood.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:15 calls the waters הַמַּיִם and the flood they could become מַבּוּל.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד הַמַּיִם לְמַבּוּל, הַמַּיִם is the subject. The promise is that the waters will never again become a flood that destroys all flesh.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial מ of מַיִם, a masculine plural common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: A body of water capable of becoming a flood.

draft.change: Clarify the Genesis 9:15 evidence by quoting the clause that describes the flood’s destructive effect.
draft.definition: An inundation in which rising waters cover the land.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 9:15, לְמַבּוּל identifies what the waters would become, and לְשַׁחֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר describes the destruction that would follow.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד הַמַּיִם לְמַבּוּל, God promises that the waters will never again become a flood. The following words לְשַׁחֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר, “to destroy all flesh,” describe what such a flood would do.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לְ marks what the waters would become after יִהְיֶה. מַבּוּל is a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67851:15, 67089:8.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ introduces the Piel infinitive construct שַׁחֵת.

analysis.evidence: In לְשַׁחֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר, “to destroy all flesh,” כָּל quantifies the collective noun בָּשָׂר. The promise concerns all flesh taken as a whole.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with בָּשָׂר as its complement.

analysis.evidence: In לְשַׁחֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר, “to destroy all flesh,” the object includes both the people addressed by the covenant and the living creatures mentioned earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It follows the construct form כָּל and has collective reference.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind
